chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Ibn Bukayr from al-Hakam ibn Abi Aqilah said:

My father gave me a house in charity, and I took possession of it. Then he had other children after that, so he wanted to take it from me and give it in charity to them. I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about that, and I informed him of the story. He said, 'Do not give it to him.' I said, 'Then he will dispute with me.' He said, 'Then dispute with him, and do not raise your voice above his voice.'

Because this charity was not permissible for him to revoke insofar as it had been taken possession of, while the first one was not like that, so it was permissible for him to change that one, and it was not permissible for him to change this one. And no one should say, 'Is not the report of Muhammad ibn Muslim, which you have presented, containing that the father's possession is possession for the minors because he is the guardian over them, and it is not permissible for him to revoke it?' And the report of Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj contains changing the charity for the minors among the children. We said, 'The report of Muhammad ibn Muslim contained that the charity for the minor children is permissible, and it does not contain that it is not permissible for him to change it.' And we, although we permitted changing this charity, did not permit its complete revocation until he transfers it to someone else and makes it for him. And we only permitted that he include with it another person whom he mentioned. And in this manner, there is no contradiction between the reports. And that which reveals the permissibility of what we mentioned is also what he narrated: 'From his wealth, then it occurs to him afterwards that he includes with him another of his children.' He said, 'There is no harm in it.'
ai.seo_question: Can a father revoke a charity gift given to his minor child to give it to other children?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the Shia jurisprudence of *sadaqah* to minors, establishing that while a father may modify the endowment by including other children, he cannot fully revoke it once the child has taken possession (*qabd*). Imam al-Sadiq (AS) advises the son to assert his right through gentle dispute (*khisamah*) rather than silence, resolving apparent contradictions in other reports by distinguishing between total revocation and permissible modification. This ruling underscores the permanence of the gift upon possession and the father's role as guardian rather than absolute owner.
